$comment: The provider-neutral SDLC contract. Each $defs entry is 1 shape that a lead, a workflow or a builder writes. It names no provider, model or tool. runtimes.json maps tiers and roles to each provider. check.js validates a value: this shape first, then the meaning. The x- keys are the shared rules that check.js reads. x-roles: the 4 roles (lead, builder, lander, reviewer) and the default tier of each; a project may map a role to its own agent type. x-tier-per-spawn: a role whose tier the spawn sets (a builder at the tier of its issue; a reviewer bounded for the diff of 1 landing, judgment as a skeptic, lead for a blind batch or a blast radius). x-first-try: a role named there first spawns at that tier for 1 mechanical step (the lander: 1 clean merge or 1 tracker read; the reviewer: the diff review of 1 landing). x-need-labels: the issue label of each capability a task may need.

x-tiers.bounded: An oracle covers every behaviour that matters. A tight brief, a file list, the signatures, 15-30 min.
x-tiers.judgment: 1 or more behaviours have no oracle, or the task has a design choice. Also a brief, a landing that steps up and a skeptic.
x-tiers.lead: The chief of staff, a blind batched review, a blast radius, and a change the step-up rule names.

task.description: The task id or part name from the brief

sha.description: The full SHA of the last pushed commit

line.description: The last output line of the focused test

red.description: Each failing test that is red on the base too (the lead passes that list), by name as the runner prints it. Only such tests may fail when passed is true

line.description: The last output line of the gate

red.description: Each failing check that is red on the base too, by name as the runner prints it. Only such checks may fail when passed is true

round.description: 0 for the first build, 1 or more for a rework round

escalation.description: Set when status is escalated. Stop and ask; do not guess.

unverified.description: Each test folder, suite or gate lane you did not run that may use your change, and each gate lane you could not run where you ran (CI is its proof). Empty when you ran them all. Do not write 'not verified' in notes instead.

extra_files.description: Every file the builder edited outside its own file list. The lander checks each against the tasks beside it that are not merged yet.

findings.description: Each problem outside the task that cost the builder time or would break main, classified. Empty or absent when none. The workflow searches the open findings and votes on a match; the builder files nothing.

severity.description: holds only when main would break: a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the command, its last output line, the file

minutes.description: The minutes the problem cost this builder

browser_s.description: Seconds the browser test runs of this agent took; 0 when none

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds this agent waited for a machine-wide browser lock before them; 0 when none

notes.description: 3 lines or fewer. Say what you did not verify.

brief.description: The builder's own short brief when the task came with none: a few lines, the approach, the traps it found, what it did not do.

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

pairs.description: A judgment for each pair of results that solve alike or clash

better.description: The id of the better result, or tie

id.description: A short unique id for the finding

evidence.description: File and line, or the command and its output

cross_issue.description: True when the problem spans 2 or more results

guard.description: true on a major that breaks a convergence guard: a second path, duplicate store or forwarder, or a second mount path

agree.description: True only if you reproduced the problem from the evidence

tracker.description: The tracker read of a flow: the output of plugin/bin/queue-state, which reads GitHub by fixed rules (no judgment), at the start and after each event. The tracker is the only state: a re-run reads it again and goes on from there. The flow decides from the facts: closed or landed is skipped; a passed report at head lands; a question goes to the lead; activity newer than x-limits.stale_claim_minutes is watched; else a builder starts, or restarts on the branch it left. A group is made ready only when every issue its PR Closes is landed and it has no open holds finding.

at.description: UTC time of the read, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

group.description: The group branch: the head of --group-pr, else <parent>-<slug> (an existing <parent>-* branch wins), or <issue>-<slug> with no parent. 1 draft PR per group.

branch.description: The task branch: the branch= of the newest trusted WORKER line on the issue, else <issue>-<slug>

tier.description: From its tier: label; judgment when none

blocked_by.description: The open issues that block it: its GitHub blocked-by links and each Blocked by #N line. Empty when none.

report.description: The newest trusted WORKER REPORT, when its first line holds passed and its head= is the remote head of its branch. Absent otherwise.

landed.description: True when the head= of the newest passed report is in origin/<group>: a run landed it already

question.description: The text of the newest trusted WORKER BLOCKED line (a question, or a landing the lander refused), or a note that the newest report lacks passed

activity_at.description: The newest WORKER LAUNCHED or STARTED comment, or commit on its branch. Absent when there is none.

body.description: The issue body, verbatim. Read only when the runtime environment has no tracker access.

pr.description: The URL of its open PR; empty when none

closes.description: Each issue the PR body Closes

holds.description: The URL of each open sev:holds finding whose body has the line Group: <group>

landing.description: 1 landing of a flow: a builder's report merged by its SHA into the group branch, the default branch merged in, the fast check run on the merge commit, and the push. CI on the push is the gate.

sha.description: The full SHA of the pushed group head; the pre-merge tip when nothing was pushed

merged.description: True when the report SHA is in the group branch and pushed

check.description: The fast check on the merge commit. Absent when the flow has no args.gate.

escalation.description: Set when merged is false: the conflict or the red check

extra_branches.description: Branches the builder pushed beside its named branch, left for the cleanup after the PR merges

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

pr.description: The draft PR of a flow group: opened at the start from the group branch with 1 Closes line per issue, 1 Closes line added for each issue that joins mid-run, and marked ready with auto-merge after its last issue landed. Every push runs the fast CI lane; ready runs the heavy lanes once.
The URL of the PR; empty when none could be opened

closes.description: Each issue the PR body has a Closes line for

ready.description: True when gh pr ready exited 0

auto_merge.description: True when gh pr merge --auto --merge exited 0

escalation.description: Set when the PR could not be opened or made ready

at.description: UTC time when the agent finished, from date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. A workflow cannot read the clock.

landing_review.description: A review of flow landings: a diff review of 1 landing (the reviewer's first-try tier), or a blind batched review of the last args.review_every landings (the reviewer tier). The review files nothing and holds nothing: the flow files or votes each finding, and only a holds finding keeps its group's PR a draft.

landings.description: The task ids of the landings the review read

findings.description: Each problem the review found in those landings, classified. Empty when none.

task.description: The task id of the landing the problem is in; 1 of landings

severity.description: holds only when main would break: a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the file and line, or the command and its last output line

minutes.description: The minutes the problem cost the reviewer; 0 when it cost none

finding.description: 1 classified finding, filed once as an issue with the labels kind:<kind> and sev:<severity>. Before filing, the agent searches the open findings; on a match it votes instead of filing. Priority = x-severity-weights[severity] x votes x minutes (at least 1). Severity holds: main would break (a red gate, a crash, data loss, a broken save, a shipped feature that stops working); only holds keeps its group's PR a draft.

evidence.description: What a second reader can check: the command, its last output line, the SHA

url.description: The URL of the finding issue, or of the open finding it voted on; empty when the filing failed

minutes.description: The minutes lost to the problem: the filing and every vote, summed

voted.description: True when an open finding matched and the agent voted on it (1 comment naming its task and the minutes lost, and a +1 reaction) instead of filing a new issue

votes.description: The votes on the finding now: 1 for the filing plus 1 per vote comment

blast.description: The output of a blast-radius check: the 1 fact a change is safe because of, and how far it was proven. level: 1 said so, 2 pointed at a file:line, 3 walked the failure step by step, 4 ran code that calls the real function, 5 reproduced in the running app.

target.description: The task id or finding id checked

proof.description: The command and its last output lines. Empty below level 4.

evidence.description: file:line, or the command and its output

cleared.description: What was checked and is fine, 1 line each

claim.description: Who owns a task. The record is an issue comment: the first line is agentic-sdlc:claim, then this object as a JSON code block. (1) The owner is the earliest claimed comment that no later released comment of the same lead cancels and no later claim supersedes. The comment's server created_at gives the order; the client field at never decides. (2) After a lead posts a claim, it reads the comments again before its first push; if it does not own the task, it posts released and stops. (3) A claim is stale when its created_at and the last commit time of the remote branch are both older than x-limits.stale_claim_minutes. (4) A new lead takes over only a stale claim: it posts a claim with supersedes and resume_sha (the remote branch head) and resumes from that SHA. If the branch is not on the remote (the old lead died before its first push), resume_sha is base_sha and only the age of the claim comment decides. (5) Every lead fetches the branch and reads the comments again before every push; it stops when a later claim supersedes it. (6) When the remote head is not a descendant of resume_sha or of the lead's own last push, someone rewrote the branch: stop and escalate.

lead.description: A stable id of the lead session

at.description: Client time, for people. The comment's created_at decides order and staleness.

supersedes.description: The URL of the stale claim comment this claim replaces

resume_sha.description: The remote branch head the new lead resumes from

claim_comment.description: 1 claim comment as the lead reads it from the issue, with the server time. The host is any GitHub host: github.com or a GitHub Enterprise Server host.

created_at.description: GitHub's created_at. It decides order and staleness.

metrics.description: 1 report row per task. A runtime that cannot measure tokens or cost writes unavailable; it never writes 0.

model.description: The model the runtime spawned, as the runtime names it

agents.description: Every agent the task started: brief, build, review share, rework

elapsed_s.description: Lead clock, from claim to integration

closed_at.description: Set when a validated merge closed the task issue and pruned its branch: the at of that merge report

pruned.description: true when the task branch and worktree are deleted; needs closed_at or reopened

reopened.description: true when the task issue closed at a validated merge and reopened because the task did not end merged; closed_at is then absent

browser_s.description: Seconds of browser test runs, summed over the reports of the task's agents

lock_wait_s.description: Seconds the task's agents waited for a machine-wide browser lock, summed over their reports

test_share.description: Test lines as a percent of test plus code lines, 1 decimal: before, on the tip before the first merge of the task; after, on the head after its last merge. Data only: no task stops on it.

reproved.description: Set when the task merged: true when a merge of the task ran its oracle again, false when each merge kept the builder's proof

runtime.description: The facts of 1 provider. A key of runtimes.json. The workflows take it as args.runtime. It has no field outside these properties: the evidence strings hold each fact and its proof.

tiers.description: Each tier to the model and effort this provider spawns

worktree_root.description: Repo-relative directory of task worktrees. Each runtime has its own root, so 2 runtimes never share a worktree directory. A remote runtime may set a placeholder that the dispatcher ignores.

agent_types.description: Each role in x-roles to the agent type name of this provider

concurrency.description: Slot cap of where the agents run, which the runtime sets (a dispatcher's slots are not the host CPUs). null: the harness decides.

capabilities.description: Each name in x-capabilities to its status and evidence. A name in x-optional-capabilities may be left out; a runtime that leaves it out does not have it.

environment.description: Optional (#331): what a builder can do where it runs, with evidence. An entry left out means a local-like builder: graphql tracker access, branch delete, no extra branches, a display. flow adapts its builder and landing prompts to it. When a runtime cannot do one, the lead injects the workaround into the brief.

access.description: graphql: gh issue view works. rest: only gh api repos/<o>/<r>/issues/<n> works. none: no tracker; the issue body goes in the prompt and the report comes back only as output.

branch_delete.description: The agent can delete a remote branch

extra_branches.description: The agent pushes a branch of its own beside the named one: land by SHA, never by branch name

display.description: The agent can take captures and run headed tests; absent moves them to the lead

remote.description: True: each agent_types entry may be a dispatcher that runs the work elsewhere (a cloud session, a remote host, another provider), waits, and returns the same schema as a local agent. Its prompts name the branch, base, brief, oracle, gate and report, never a path under worktree_root. The host load does not apply: concurrency and the slot cap limit where the agents run. Absent or false: the agents run on the workflow host.

verified.description: False: the model id or effort is a guess. check.js lists it.

status.description: enforced: the runtime refuses a breach. instructed: only the prompt asks for it.
